_about: Keys, locks and enemies. Worlds 3-4 only; chapter 1 places none of this.
EVERY NUMBER IS A GUESS. The structure below is DATA, read from the level files:
- No enemy is ever placed directly in a scene. Every minion, boss and projectile is
script-spawned from an invisible marker, which is why the data has minion_spawn
markers and zero minion instances. 60 spawners across 35 levels: 28 in world 3,
- waypointName is a PREFIX, not a name: 'wayA' means patrol wayA0 <-> wayA1.
- holdTime is MILLISECONDS. A lone wayX0 with a sentinel hold of 9999999 is how the
designers authored a STATIONARY GUARD - so one resolved waypoint means 'stand
still', not 'data missing'. Clamped rather than taken literally.
- Minions carry breakable, burnable AND teleportable, all set. They are puzzle
objects as much as threats: crushable by a rolling stone, burnable, or portalled
off the level onto enemy_killer - an invisible solid kill floor below the bounds
of every world-3 level. That is what the 'Kill all minions' achievements are for.
- Keys pair with keyholes and locked doors BY COLOUR (yellow 33 / blue 6 / red 2 per
role, identical multisets per level), never by proximity: a keyhole and its door
- There is NO physics contact callback for a key in the binary; pickup is distance-
polled from a per-frame update, so it is a range test rather than an overlap.

key._note: Ranges invented. The colour pairing they operate on is DATA.

_note: Sight drives the 'without getting noticed by any minion' achievements, so range and
occlusion matter to scoring - but neither number is measured. The original occludes
sight with anti_sight_wall.ent, an invisible bar; modelled here as a physics raycast
against level geometry, which is the closest honest equivalent.
SUPERSEDED by planning step 158 (G1a): the port's sight is built from the original's decoded
findEntityInSight (three 128-unit buckets of the knight's row, a 120 degree cone, a ray that every
body but the knights' and the player's blocks) and its numbers are game/data/minions.json `sight`.
sight_range_px below is an invented guess nothing reads; it is kept only so this old table still
